levels.3: L3 SaaS or portal (accounts, APIs, dashboards)

how.passive_http: One read-only GET/HEAD against your own site. Result measured.
how.passive_dns: DNS, RDAP or certificate transparency lookup. Result measured.
how.passive_tcp_targeted: Reachability of a fixed list of ports that must never be public. No port sweep.
how.content_parse: Read from the page we already fetched. No extra request.
how.perf_sample: Measured from the live request timing and payload size.
how.internal_access: Needs admin or cloud console access. Not visible from outside.
how.human_review: Needs a person to judge it. Reported as a consultant review item.
how.external_service: Needs a third-party data source this tool does not call.
how.interview: Asked in Step 3 as a business fact, not scanned from the site.

infra.title: Website & infrastructure
items: Whois must show your own SSM entity, not a freelance email.
A lapsed domain takes email and the website down together.
Slow TTL slows every later fix.
Where the server sits decides MY latency and data residency.
AAAA pointing at a mail host breaks sending for some networks.
Services reachable that should never be public
Database and admin ports on the open internet are an instant breach path.
Web server software and version disclosed
Version banners hand attackers a matching exploit list.
Old TLS or an untrusted chain triggers browser warnings.
An expired certificate turns every page into a security warning.
Without enforcement, sessions are readable on the first hop.
Missing headers let clickjacking and MIME sniffing through.
No HSTS means a downgrade is still possible.
No CSP means any injected script runs in the visitor's browser.
A reflecting origin lets any website read your logged-in data.
Unflagged session cookies travel in the clear and cross sites.
Index of / exposes uploads, backups and internal paths.
One forgotten .zip is your whole customer list.
A public .env usually contains live database and API credentials.
Public .git rebuilds source plus deleted secrets.
Debug routes dump config, queries and stack traces.
Admin panel reachable from the internet
We only note reachability; we never attempt a login.
stage.example.com often runs with old code and no hardening.
Old HTTP/1.1 slows every mobile visitor.
Mixed content (http assets on https page)
Browsers show a broken padlock even on an https page.
Two live hosts split your SEO and confuse certificate coverage.
Without these anyone can send an invoice carrying your domain.

vuln.title: Web vulnerabilities
items: Matched against OSV, CISA KEV and endoflife.date, not guessed.
Out-of-support PHP or WordPress core receives no security fixes.
xmlrpc and readme files are the standard first probes.
Abandoned plugins are the top malware entry point on WP.
Web application firewall in front of the site
A WAF buys time while the underlying software gets patched.
Open redirect on login or outbound links
We list candidate parameters; validating them needs an authorised test.

auth.title: Authentication
items: Nothing to check below if there is no login at all.
Open signup plus weak controls is an abuse surface.
Visible only from inside the account flow.
An admin login without MFA is the most common entry point.
Requires a real account to observe.
Reset page presence is visible; token strength is not.
Detects the token format; validation flaws need authorised testing.
Session and token revocation on logout

data.title: Data and secrets exposure
items: API keys published in page or scripts
A key in client code is anyone's key; rotate on sight.
AKIA or connection strings in JS mean account takeover.
Connection strings must never sit in a served file.
Password or secret fields hardcoded in HTML
Defaults in markup are effectively published credentials.
Personally identifiable data on public pages
IC numbers, customer lists or staff emails on a page get scraped by brokers within days.
Source maps served to the browser
Verbose errors or stack traces served
Framework error pages leak paths, versions and sometimes keys.
Published storage bucket with listing allowed
Only buckets your own pages reference are checked, read-only.
A public .sql is every customer record.
A business decision, not a scan result.
Asked in Step 3; a customer can demand their record be removed.

api.title: API surface
items: Only what your own pages reference is listed.
Introspection on by default is a free API map.
Realtime channels need their own auth story.
Public JSON is inspectable; private responses are not.
Unversioned APIs cannot be retired safely.
Old paths often skip current auth.
Debug routes are meant to be internal.
Public docs are a scripted attack map; decide deliberately.
Verbose JSON errors leak paths and versions.
Asked in Step 3; nobody scans their way to an inventory.
Every embedded service is part of your attack surface.

cloud.title: Cloud and hosting
items: You cannot secure what is not on the list.
Load balancer in front of origin
Single origin plus no health check means one machine is your uptime.
Edge caching removes most of the load from your origin.
Published URLs point at buckets that may be world-readable.
Only buckets referenced by your pages are queried.
Console visibility; a public DB port shows up in the port check.
Shared hosting with root access nobody exercises is the common failure.
Functions shift patching duty but add IAM duty.
Orchestrators need their own hardening baseline.
IAM users and access keys inventory
A leaked JSON key bypasses every other control.
A policy question, asked in Step 3.
Asked in Step 3; ex-staff retaining access is common.
Verified by a restore drill, not by a checkbox.
Fixed list of known consoles; no range scanning.
Origin IP concealed behind the edge
A published origin IP lets attackers bypass the WAF entirely.

crm.title: CRM and customer data
items: Where customer records start, so it is the isolation boundary.
Marks the boundary the authorisation checks apply to.
Profile endpoints are the usual IDOR target.
Recovery is the most commonly bypassed authentication path.
No ticket route means support lives in personal WhatsApp.
Search endpoints leak records when unguarded.
Shared invoice or quote pages leak contact data.
Without a trail you cannot prove who saw or promised what.
Asked in Step 3; the reason records must be company-owned.

ecom.title: E-commerce and payments
items: WooCommerce, Shopify or Magento changes the patching duty.
Nothing below applies without a cart.
Hosted checkout beats capturing card data yourself.
Invoice or order page reachable by ID
Ask your developer whether order numbers are sequential; we do not open anyone's document to test it.

biz.title: Business: positioning, conversion and trust
items: A parked, under-construction or near-empty page reads as a company that is gone.
Company identity stated on the homepage
A visitor must know who they are dealing with in seconds.
If the offer is not on the page, it does not exist.
Trade buyers self-select only when they see themselves.
Features get skimmed; outcomes get enquired.
Reason to choose you over others
Without differentiation the price conversation is all there is.
Primary call to action above the fold
Traffic without a next step is wasted traffic.
Phone, email and address all present and clickable.
No form means no structured lead capture at all.
For trade buyers this is the whole point of the site.
Malaysian buyers expect it; without it you lose the quick question.
Mobile journey usable end to end
Most SME traffic is mobile-only; a broken form loses it silently.
Recognisable names do the trust work for you.
Proof beats adjectives for repeat purchase businesses.
Named and specific beats glowing and vague.
Third-party validation costs nothing to display.
Tender buyers filter on certificates before they call.
Partnership logos signal an established supplier.
Photos of installed work outperform stock imagery.
Any claim without a number reads as decoration.
No analytics means no idea which page earns.
Tag governance without a developer in the loop.
Ad spend without conversion events is guesswork.
The most valuable event is usually unmeasured.
Tells you which offer actually pulls.
Without steps you cannot see where buyers drop.
Asked in Step 3; the honest answer is usually no.
Website leads land in a system
Asked in Step 3; a form that posts to nobody is theatre.

seo.title: SEO and indexability
items: The title is the search result; missing means Google writes it.
Free copy that decides whether the click happens.
Structure tells the crawler what the page is about.
Skipped headings read as a lazily built page.
Duplicates split your rankings and confuse indexes.
Without it new pages get found late or never.
A wrong directive can block the whole site silently.
A 404 on a quote page is a lost customer.
Schema is how machines read your business.
Name, logo and sameAs links build the entity Google knows.
Eligibility for rich results on product searches.
Answers the buyer already typed into Google.
Also the accessibility check large buyers ask for.
Every second costs a share of mobile visitors.
Mobile-first indexing makes this a ranking factor too.
Needs a browser lab; we report TTFB and weight instead.
A stray noindex hides a finished website.
Oversized pages lose mobile buyers on metered data.

ai.title: AI adoption and AI safety
items: Live chat or AI assistant on site
Nobody answering after hours is where enquiries go to die.
Catalogue depth needs search that understands parts codes.
Repetitive questions are exactly what automation is for.
A qualified lead saved before a human sees it.
Cross-sell on a site that already has the traffic.
Asked in Step 3; the biggest time sink in trade SMEs.
AI wired into a customer database
Without structured data, AI answers are guesses.
Only meaningful once traffic is worth segmenting.
Tool permissions are visible only from the configuration.
Needs the agent config, not the website.
Customer data sent to a model
Asked in Step 3; whatever you feed a model stops being yours to control.
A key in page source funds someone else's usage.
Requires reviewing what the agent is allowed to do.
Needed to reconstruct who was told what.
Whether AI assistants can read your catalogue at all.
Name, address and registration must agree everywhere.
Internal part codes are meaningless to search and models.
PDF-only catalogues are invisible to answer engines.
Structured data is the precondition for AI surfacing.
Needs a search data source this tool does not call.
Needs a provider query we deliberately do not send.
Same limitation; consultant can verify manually.

content.title: Content, trust and legal
items: Only you or your engineer can confirm specifications.
A stale copyright year reads as an abandoned company.
Broken contact page costs leads nobody reports to you.
Buttons wired to a real destination
Dead CTAs look like design until you count the lost clicks.
Trade buyers check a physical address before they trust a quote.
Consistent third-party presence corroborates the entity.
Once the site collects names and numbers, buyers and partners ask for the notice.
Disputes are cheaper when the terms were shown.
Required once analytics and pixels are loaded.
Tender and corporate buyers verify before shortlisting.
Three spellings dilute search and trust.
Unbacked superlatives read as noise to a trade buyer.
Named clients and real numbers are what make them land.

perf.title: Performance and availability
items: Slow first byte is server-side, not visitor-side.
Mobile buyers bounce before a heavy page paints.
Unresized photos are the usual weight culprit.
Theme bundling often ships three frameworks.
Edge cache turns one server into a global one.
No cache headers means every visit rebuilds the page.
A white error page is a lost buyer plus a leaked stack trace.
Only an observation from this network at this time.
DDoS absorption in front of origin
Visible from the edge provider you resolve to.
Asked in Step 3; untested backups are a rumour.
